Hi Sarah,

Following our discovery call, the Eng/Infra team at Acme asked for a technical deep-dive on Dedicated capacity (pool sizing, autoscaling, and isolation). We usually run a 60- to 75-minute session that covers:
- short workload profile review (we'll bring a short model/sequence-length primer)
- pool topology and sizing guidance
- autoscaling behavior and knobs (throttles, burst, warm pools)
- isolation and multi-tenant guardrails + failover plan
- Q&A and next steps (MVP config + trial plan)

Proposed times (PT):
- Tue Jan 20, 10:00–11:15
- Wed Jan 21, 14:00–15:15
- Thu Jan 22, 09:30–10:45

Can you confirm who from Acme will join (platform lead, infra, SRE?) and which slot works best? I attached our one-pager and a sample pool-sizing spreadsheet for context.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_capacity_overview.pdf (one-pager), pool-sizing-proposal.pdf (template)

Thanks,
Soojin Lee

Thanks — small change on our side: we have a conflicting exec review on Jan 20. Could we move to Wed Jan 21 at 14:00 PT instead? A 60-minute slot should be fine.

Expected targets for context: steady-state concurrency ~40 concurrent requests per region, peak bursts up to ~250 concurrent (short spikes). Target p95 latency for user-facing calls is 150–200ms (token-level varies by model). Cross-region failover is allowed but needs to respect data residency — we can discuss acceptable patterns.

I'll upload the workload spreadsheet to the shared Drive and add a short notes doc: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ExamplePreRead
